A_target.statement: The [[Definition:2-Satisfiability Problem|2-satisfiability problem]], for a [[Definition:Conjunctive Normal Form|CNF]] formula with two literals per clause, is decidable in time linear in the size of the formula.

B_source.statement:
Let $D$ be a [[Definition:Directed Graph|directed graph]].
Then the [[Definition:Strongly Connected Component|strongly connected components]] of $D$ can be computed in time $\map O {\card V + \card E}$.

substitutions.the vertices of the digraph: the literals, each variable and its negation
substitutions.the directed edges: the two implications equivalent to each clause
substitutions.a strongly connected component: a set of literals forced to share a truth value

derived.a variable and its negation in one compo: a contradiction, so the formula is unsatisfiable
derived.the reverse topological order of compone: an assignment satisfying the formula when no contradiction occurs

object_map.reformulation: Encode each clause as a pair of implications, turning satisfiability into a reachability question on a digraph.

validity_conditions: Each two-literal clause is logically equivalent to a pair of implications, so the graph faithfully encodes the formula with size linear in it.
Literals in one strongly connected component imply one another and so must share a truth value; a variable together with its negation in one component is therefore a contradiction.
When no such contradiction occurs, assigning each component by reverse topological order yields a consistent satisfying assignment, since implications never point from true to false.
proof_plan: Build the [[Definition:Implication Graph|implication graph]] on the literals: for each clause $a \lor b$, add edges $\neg a \to b$ and $\neg b \to a$.
By [[Tarjan's Algorithm]], compute the strongly connected components in linear time.

If $x$ and $
eg x$ lie in the same component, then $x \implies 
eg x$ and $
eg x \implies x$ are both forced, so the formula is unsatisfiable.
